title: SD Bullion vs JM Bullion: Buying and Selling Compared
summary: SD Bullion vs JM Bullion side by side: card vs cash prices, free shipping, selling back, minimums and payout times, all checked on each dealer's own site.
body_markdown:
SD Bullion and JM Bullion mostly look alike. Both give a 4% discount for paying by a cash method instead of a card. Both ship free at around $199. The real differences show up when you sell back to them. JM Bullion lets you lock a sell price online with a $1,000 minimum; SD Bullion locks prices over the phone, with minimums set by weight. One disclosure up front: we run Pure, a[marketplace for gold and silver](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace) where buyers and sellers set their own prices, so we have a stake in this topic. Pure comes up once, near the end. Every dealer detail below is from SD Bullion's and JM Bullion's own websites as of November 18, 2026, and either can change its terms, so check their sites before you order.

## Paying for an Order: Card vs Cash Prices


Both dealers price for cash first. Pay by card, lose the 4%.


At JM Bullion, the 4% applies to paper checks and eCheck (ACH) up to $100,000, plus bank wires anywhere from $500 all the way up to $1,000,000. Crypto gets 3%. Cards and PayPal get no discount, though they're accepted on orders up to $250,000. Klarna covers orders from $35 to $30,000.


SD Bullion caps card orders at $5,000 and PayPal at $500. Neither gets the cash discount. E-checks, which link your checking account to your SD Bullion profile, are eligible for the 4% on orders up to $10,000; SD Bullion notes that it doesn't accept ACH as a payment method. Personal checks are accepted up to $20,000. Bank wire isn't offered under $2,500, and above $20,000 it's the only method accepted.


Over $5,000 on a card, it's JM. Cash gets 4% off at both.


## Shipping and Free-Shipping Minimums


Shipping is close to a tie. SD Bullion ships and insures domestic orders over $199 for free, with that line measured on the cash discount price, not on what the same order would cost you by card. Below it, $9.95 flat. JM Bullion ships orders of $199 or more for free. Every package it sends carries full third-party shipping insurance, according to its shipping page, which doesn't list a charge for smaller orders.


## Selling Back to Each Dealer


The two split here.


JM Bullion's Sell To Us page says you can lock your price online, 24 hours a day, without talking to anyone. Its buyback prices for most of its popular products are published right on the site, so you can see the number before you decide to sell, whatever time it is. There's a $1,000 minimum.


SD Bullion does it by phone. The premiums on its sell page are indications only. Prices aren't locked in until you call the buyback team and lock a trade. Minimums go by weight: 40 ounces of silver, 2 ounces of gold, 1 ounce each of platinum or palladium. Once it receives your package, its inventory team inspects each item for authenticity.


If you'd rather not get on the phone, that difference alone may decide it. Check the minimums too. A single 1 oz gold coin falls under SD Bullion's 2-ounce gold minimum. A handful of silver coins can fall under JM Bullion's $1,000.


## Getting Paid After You Sell


JM Bullion's page carries two different timings. Its Sell To Us page says payments are issued 3 to 7 business days after it receives your product. The same page also carries a notice that, "due to current market conditions," payment is being issued 10 or more business days after receipt. Payout options are ACH at no fee, a bank wire for $25, or a paper check for $50.


SD Bullion's sell page says payment is issued within 1 to 3 business days after processing. Its sellback FAQ puts most ACH payments at 3 to 5 business days, while a bank wire, which costs $30, can take 24 to 48 hours to land in your account.


Ask before you ship.


## Which One Fits Which Buyer


JM Bullion fits two kinds of people: buyers who want to pay a large order by card or PayPal, and sellers who'd like to lock a price online at midnight without ever picking up the phone. Its minimum is flat: $1,000.


SD Bullion suits cash buyers who are happy paying by e-check or wire, plus sellers who would rather talk a trade through with a real person on the phone than click through a form. Weigh what you have first.


Nothing stops you from using both.


## A Third Option: Buying and Selling on a Marketplace


Both of these are dealers. They sell at prices they set and buy back at prices they quote. Pure works differently. It's a marketplace where buyers and sellers post their own prices on each product's order book: you can take the lowest ask or post a bid and wait. On the sell side you can sell into the highest bid, which fills right away, or post an ask at the price you want. There's no minimum to sell. Sellers pay a published fee of 0.5% to 1.5% depending on the item and their quarterly volume; buyers pay no marketplace fee. Seller payouts go out automatically once an item checks in and passes verification, about 3 business days from check-in by ACH or check. Shipping to buyers is $25 on orders under $10,000 and free from $10,000.


The[Pure marketplace](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace) shows the live bids and asks without an account.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Which Is Better for Selling, SD Bullion or JM Bullion?


It depends on what you're selling and how you want to lock the price. JM Bullion takes sell orders online with a $1,000 minimum. SD Bullion locks prices by phone, with minimums of 40 ounces of silver, 2 ounces of gold, or 1 ounce of platinum or palladium.


### Do SD Bullion and JM Bullion Charge More for Credit Cards?


Both list a 4% cash discount that cards don't get, so a card order costs more than the same order paid by a cash method. SD Bullion also caps card orders at $5,000; JM Bullion takes cards up to $250,000.


### Does Either Dealer Offer Free Shipping?


Both do. SD Bullion's line is orders over $199, measured on the cash price, with $9.95 charged below it. JM's is $199 or more.


### Can You Sell Coins to SD Bullion or JM Bullion Online?


At JM Bullion, yes: its Sell To Us page lets you lock a price online at any hour. SD Bullion's sell page lists buyback premiums it calls indications only; the price locks over the phone.
